paragraphs: When several linear prediction problems have correlated noise, estimating them together can be more effective than treating each separately. The challenge is that both the prediction coefficients and the noise covariance are unknown. Alternating minimization updates these quantities in turn, but the resulting joint estimation problem is nonconvex, making its observed effectiveness difficult to justify theoretically.

This paper analyzes alternating minimization without requiring fresh observations at every iteration. That change matters because earlier analyses assumed repeated access to new samples, leaving a gap between their guarantees and procedures that reuse one dataset. The authors focus on high-dimensional models whose coefficients have an assumed structure, and express statistical error using Gaussian width, a measure connected to that structure.

The analysis also shows that random initialization can achieve the same performance as a carefully initialized procedure for this regression problem. Experiments support the theoretical results. Together, these findings strengthen the explanation for why alternating estimation can work while reusing data and avoiding a specially prepared starting point.
neurips-2018-an-improved-analysis-of-alt.tldr: A resampling-free analysis explains how alternating minimization can estimate structured multi-response regressions effectively even from random initialization.

paragraphs: Adversarial training tries to make a neural network withstand deliberately difficult inputs. Many defenses optimize against a single estimate of the worst attack permitted by predefined constraints. The paper identifies a vulnerability in this approach: a stronger adversary encountered during testing may fall beyond those constraints, and robustness can then deteriorate sharply.

The proposed Bayesian framework represents uncertainty about the adversary itself. Instead of committing to one adversarial data-generating distribution, it places a probability distribution over such distributions. This uncertainty lets training account for potential adversaries stronger than the point estimate used in distributionally robust optimization. The framework also incorporates uncertainty about the network's parameters.

To make this Bayesian treatment computationally usable, the authors design a scalable Markov Chain Monte Carlo strategy for sampling the parameter posterior. They report experiments supporting improvements over existing adversarial training methods. The contribution is therefore both a broader representation of adversarial uncertainty and a practical inference strategy, with the reported robustness gains established experimentally.
neurips-2018-bayesian-adversarial-learni.tldr: Bayesian adversarial learning models uncertainty about both attackers and network parameters to improve robustness beyond a single estimated worst-case attack.

paragraphs: Pose graph optimization appears in tasks such as reconstructing structure from images and simultaneously estimating location and mapping an environment. A useful solution needs reliable initial poses, while an uncertainty estimate can indicate how much confidence to place in those poses. This paper develops a method that addresses both needs within one computational framework.

The method, Tempered Geodesic Markov Chain Monte Carlo, combines global nonconvex optimization with posterior sampling. It operates on the spherical geometry of quaternions used to represent rotations. Bringing optimization and sampling together allows it to provide starting poses for pose graph optimization while also describing uncertainty about the solution, rather than returning only a single estimate.

The authors establish theoretical convergence guarantees and evaluate the method on synthetic and real benchmarks. They report robustness to missing observations and noise, and find that the uncertainty estimates reflect intuitive properties of the data. These results support using the method both to initialize optimization and to assess the quality of the resulting pose estimates.
neurips-2018-bayesian-pose-graph-optimiz.tldr: Tempered Geodesic MCMC combines pose initialization with posterior sampling to provide reliable starting estimates and informative uncertainty.

paragraphs: Group-sparse regression encourages predictors to be selected or suppressed in groups. Its usefulness therefore depends on how those groups are defined. Most methods assume the grouping is supplied in advance, but that information may be unavailable or unsuitable. This paper treats the group structure as something to estimate from data.

The authors formulate this estimation as a continuous bilevel optimization problem using separate training and validation data. The two levels connect fitting the regression model with learning its grouping structure. To make the nested optimization tractable, they replace the lower-level problem with an approximation based on a smooth dual forward-backward algorithm using Bregman distances.

The paper provides guarantees that relate the approximate procedure to the exact problem as the approximation converges. Synthetic experiments demonstrate favorable behavior, and a preliminary application to gene expression data explores the discovery of functional groups. The contribution is a way to learn the structure controlling regularization, supported by convergence analysis and initial empirical evidence.
neurips-2018-bilevel-learning-of-the-gro.tldr: A bilevel optimization method learns the grouping structure used by group-sparse regression instead of requiring it in advance.

paragraphs: Channel pruning compresses a neural network by removing some of its feature channels. The paper argues that two common approaches have drawbacks: training with channel sparsity can be expensive and difficult to converge, while matching a pretrained network's feature maps can overlook whether retained channels actually help distinguish classes. Preserving intermediate features is not by itself the same objective as preserving classification ability.

The proposed method adds losses that encourage intermediate layers to become more discriminative. It then selects channels using both these losses and the error in reconstructing the original feature maps. A greedy procedure alternates between channel selection and parameter optimization, tying compression decisions to the network's predictive task.

Experiments support the method's effectiveness. On ILSVRC-12, the authors report that a ResNet-50 with 30% fewer channels exceeds the original model's top-1 accuracy by 0.39%. This example shows that their task-aware selection can remove substantial channel capacity while preserving, and in this case improving, measured classification performance.
neurips-2018-discrimination-aware-channe.tldr: Discrimination-aware pruning selects channels for their contribution to classification as well as feature reconstruction, enabling effective network compression.

paragraphs: Forecasting treatment response from health records is complicated because treatment choices depend on a patient's changing condition. Those same changing variables can also influence the eventual outcome. Consequently, directly learning associations between treatments and outcomes can mix treatment effects with the reasons a treatment was selected.

The paper introduces the Recurrent Marginal Structural Network, a sequence-to-sequence model that predicts expected responses to a planned sequence of treatments. Its approach draws on marginal structural models, which use propensity weighting to adjust for time-dependent confounding. Combining this causal adjustment idea with a sequential architecture addresses both treatment-selection bias and the evolution of responses over time.

The authors evaluate the method using simulations from a pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic model of tumor growth. In those simulations, the network accurately learns unbiased treatment responses from observational data, including when treatment-assignment policies change, and improves on benchmarks. These findings support its ability to forecast under changing assignment rules in the studied simulation setting; the reported evaluation is not a clinical deployment.
neurips-2018-forecasting-treatment-respo.tldr: A recurrent forecasting model uses ideas from propensity weighting to learn treatment responses despite time-dependent confounding in tumor-growth simulations.

paragraphs: Comparing two models against observed data often calls for more than a single ranking. A useful comparison can also identify where one model captures the data better. This paper develops two statistical tests for relative goodness of fit that combine a model comparison with interpretable evidence about the source of the difference.

The tests are nonparametric and have runtime that grows linearly with the number of samples. Their distinguishing feature is the ability to return informative examples indicating regions of the data domain where one model fits significantly better than its competitor. This connects a statistical conclusion to concrete parts of the observations that help explain it.

In a real-world comparison of generative adversarial networks, the reported test matches the statistical power of a state-of-the-art relative-fit test while running about ten times faster. That result supports the practical value of combining efficiency with interpretation: the comparison can retain sensitivity to model differences while also helping users locate those differences.
neurips-2018-informative-features-for-mo.tldr: Two efficient statistical tests compare model fit and identify informative examples showing where one model performs significantly better.

paragraphs: A neural network can have enough capacity to memorize arbitrary labels yet still learn predictions that generalize. This paper investigates that tension theoretically for a two-layer ReLU network used in multiclass classification. It studies stochastic gradient descent starting from random initialization in an overparameterized setting, where the network has more capacity than would be needed simply to fit the task.

The key assumption concerns the structure of the observations: they come from a mixture of well-separated distributions. Under this setting, the authors prove that stochastic gradient descent learns a network with small generalization error. The guarantee therefore connects successful learning to the combination of data structure, network capacity, and the training algorithm.

The result helps explain why the ability to fit arbitrary labels need not prevent learning useful patterns on structured data. The analysis also offers insights into aspects of neural-network learning that can be examined empirically using synthetic data and MNIST. Its theoretical claim remains tied to the specified network and separated-mixture setting.
neurips-2018-learning-overparameterized-.tldr: For well-separated mixture data, SGD can train an overparameterized two-layer ReLU network from random initialization to achieve small generalization error.

paragraphs: The paper introduces Legendre decomposition, a method for representing a nonnegative tensor through a multiplicative combination of parameters. A tensor is a multidimensional array, so the task is to reconstruct such an array using a parameterized representation. The method makes the quality and uniqueness of that reconstruction central to its formulation.

Its mathematical foundation comes from information geometry. Within the proposed decomposition, the reconstructed tensor is unique and minimizes the Kullback–Leibler divergence from the input tensor. This gives a precise meaning to the preferred reconstruction: it is selected by a specified measure of discrepancy, with a uniqueness guarantee for the reconstructed array.

The authors also compare reconstruction quality empirically with other nonnegative tensor decomposition methods and report that Legendre decomposition can be more accurate. The theoretical and empirical claims address different aspects of the contribution. The theory characterizes the reconstruction selected by the method, while the experiments support its usefulness relative to alternative decompositions in the comparisons studied.
neurips-2018-legendre-decomposition-for-.tldr: Legendre decomposition provides a unique KL-minimizing tensor reconstruction and shows empirical accuracy advantages over other nonnegative decompositions.

paragraphs: A scene graph describes an image through its objects and the relationships between them. Producing one requires recognizing individual objects while understanding how they relate to the rest of the scene. LinkNet addresses this by explicitly modeling dependencies across object instances, so the representation of an object can incorporate its connections to others.

The central component is a relational embedding module that jointly represents connections among related objects. The authors report that this improves both object classification and relationship classification. Added to a basic Faster R-CNN, the approach achieves state-of-the-art results on Visual Genome, showing that relational information can strengthen both parts of scene graph generation.

The final model also includes modules for global scene context and geometric layout, which further improve performance. Extensive ablation studies evaluate the model's components and support its effectiveness. The overall contribution is an architecture that combines relationships, scene-wide information, and spatial arrangement when building a structured description of an image.
neurips-2018-linknet-relational-embeddin.tldr: LinkNet improves scene graph generation by jointly representing object relationships, global context, and geometric layout.

paragraphs: Sampling-based probabilistic inference often depends on carefully designed proposals for moving between possible model states. Constructing those proposals by hand for each model can require substantial effort. This paper learns proposal mechanisms that can transfer across models, aiming to reuse inference knowledge wherever common structural patterns appear.

The authors parameterize proposals with neural networks that quickly approximate block Gibbs conditional distributions. These proposals operate on groups of variables and generalize across recurring structural motifs. The resulting idea is a library of learned inference primitives: reusable components that can accelerate inference in previously unseen models without training specifically for each new model.

The paper explores several applications. In open-universe Gaussian mixture models, the learned proposals outperform a manually tuned sampler. In a real-world named entity recognition task, the sampler achieves higher final F1 scores than classical single-site Gibbs sampling. These findings support the usefulness of transferring learned sampling behavior across shared model structures, with benefits demonstrated in both probabilistic modeling and a language task.
neurips-2018-meta-learning-mcmc-proposal.tldr: Neural MCMC proposals learned for recurring model structures can accelerate inference on unseen models without model-specific training.

paragraphs: This paper studies how multiple agents can collaboratively evaluate a given policy when they jointly observe state-action pairs but receive private local rewards. The task is to estimate the policy's value through decentralized cooperation. Complex interactions between agents make this harder than evaluating a policy with a single learner.

The proposed algorithm combines two kinds of averaging. Averaging across neighboring agents incorporates gradient information from elsewhere in the network, while averaging over time incorporates local reward information. The authors derive this procedure by reformulating mean squared Bellman error minimization as a primal-dual problem, producing a decentralized convex-concave saddle-point formulation.

They prove that the resulting algorithm reaches the optimal solution at a global geometric rate. This provides a fast finite-time convergence result for the decentralized optimization problem underlying policy evaluation. The paper presents this as, to the authors' knowledge, the first such fast result for decentralized convex-concave saddle-point problems. Its contribution concerns evaluating a supplied policy under the stated information-sharing arrangement.
neurips-2018-multi-agent-reinforcement-l.tldr: A decentralized policy-evaluation algorithm averages information across agents and time and has a proven global geometric convergence rate.

paragraphs: This paper introduces the Neural Tangent Kernel, or NTK, to describe how a neural network's predictions evolve during gradient-based training. Instead of tracking every parameter individually, the kernel describes the network's changing input-output function. This extends the connection between neural networks and kernel methods beyond their behavior at initialization.

For finite networks, the NTK is initially random and changes during training. In the infinite-width limit, the authors prove that it approaches an explicit kernel that remains fixed. This makes training dynamics accessible in function space, and connects convergence to whether the limiting kernel is positive definite.

For least-squares regression in that limit, the prediction function follows a linear differential equation. Learning proceeds fastest along the largest principal components defined by the NTK, suggesting a theoretical motivation for early stopping. Numerical studies examine wide networks and compare their kernels with the infinite-width limit. The fixed-kernel result is specifically a limiting description, while the numerical work explores its relationship to finite, wide networks.
neurips-2018-neural-tangent-kernel-conve.tldr: The Neural Tangent Kernel describes network training dynamics and becomes fixed at infinite width, enabling a kernel-based analysis of convergence.

paragraphs: Leverage score sampling offers a way to approximate computations involving large matrices while adapting the computational effort to the problem's structure. Its attraction is that a carefully chosen sample can retain information needed for a faithful approximation. The difficulty is that obtaining the sampling probabilities can itself be expensive and require approximation.

This paper addresses that difficulty for positive definite matrices defined by a kernel. Its first contribution is a new algorithm for leverage score sampling. Its second is a kernel ridge regression solver that uses the proposed sampling method, connecting the matrix approximation problem directly to a statistical learning task.

The main technical result establishes efficiency and accuracy advantages for these algorithms, which the authors describe as the strongest available for the problems considered. The contribution therefore concerns both generating useful samples and turning them into an effective learning procedure. It targets the computational work needed to obtain the approximation, as well as the quality of the resulting solution.
neurips-2018-on-fast-leverage-score-samp.tldr: A new leverage score sampling algorithm supports an efficient kernel ridge regression solver with technical guarantees on efficiency and accuracy.

paragraphs: Wasserstein-based GANs compare generated and real data distributions using a distance with appealing modeling properties. Optimizing that distance is difficult, however, because the objective is nonconvex, nonsmooth, and hard to compute. This paper studies a smoothed formulation based on regularized optimal transport as a way to make training more tractable.

The authors show that gradient information for the smoothed objective is easy to obtain computationally, making first-order optimization applicable. They establish convergence to stationarity for a proposed class of GAN training algorithms. A useful feature is that the discriminator only needs to be solved approximately, rather than to exact optimality.

Experiments generate MNIST digits and CIFAR-10 images. The method is reported to be computationally efficient and to produce images comparable to state-of-the-art methods when architecture and computational power are held equal. The theoretical result concerns reaching stationarity, while the empirical results address the practical quality and efficiency of generated images under those matched resources.
neurips-2018-on-the-convergence-and-robu.tldr: Regularized optimal transport makes GAN gradients tractable and supports convergence to stationarity with only approximately optimized discriminators.

paragraphs: Subsampling reduces the computational burden of fitting statistical models to large datasets. Choosing observations with unequal probabilities can be useful, but many models lack a principled rule for deciding which observations deserve greater sampling probability. This paper derives such a rule using the estimator's influence function, which describes how individual observations affect the estimate.

The derivation applies to asymptotically linear estimators and yields asymptotically optimal sampling probabilities for a broad class of popular models. The authors distinguish this tight optimality result from guarantees that provide only probabilistic error bounds or optimal rates. The strength of the claim is asymptotic and tied to the estimator framework they analyze.

For linear regression, the paper also compares the method empirically with existing nonuniform subsampling procedures. It reports better performance even when using approximations to the optimal probabilities. This connects the theoretical sampling rule to a practical implementation: useful gains can remain when the ideal sampling probabilities are not calculated exactly.
neurips-2018-optimal-subsampling-with-in.tldr: Influence functions yield asymptotically optimal subsampling probabilities, with empirical improvements for linear regression even using approximate probabilities.

paragraphs: This paper introduces Spike-and-Slab Deep Learning, a fully Bayesian alternative to dropout for regularizing deep ReLU networks. Its central question is whether a network can recover a smooth input-output relationship without knowing in advance how smooth that relationship is. That unknown smoothness normally affects the architecture needed for optimal performance.

The authors prove that the posterior concentrates around alpha-Hölder smooth maps at a near-minimax rate. In other words, the uncertainty represented by the posterior narrows around the target at a rate close to the best achievable for the smoothness class. The construction adapts to unknown smoothness, performing as well as if its level had been supplied beforehand.

The analysis also informs the choice of network depth, width, and sparsity. Rather than requiring these attributes to be tuned using known smoothness, the Bayesian construction addresses that dependence. The paper further shows that the posterior favors smaller networks with up to the optimal number of nodes and links, giving a specific theoretical sense in which the method avoids overfitting.
neurips-2018-posterior-concentration-for.tldr: Spike-and-Slab Deep Learning provides near-minimax Bayesian recovery of smooth functions while adapting to unknown smoothness and favoring appropriately sparse networks.

paragraphs: The paper introduces quadratic decomposable submodular function minimization, a convex optimization problem connected to learning on graphs and hypergraphs. Relevant settings include graph-based semi-supervised learning and PageRank. Its contribution is to identify this optimization formulation and develop an efficient method for solving it, with both convergence analysis and learning experiments.

The authors approach the problem through a new dual formulation. This produces an objective that can be optimized using random coordinate descent together with projections onto cones. They establish a linear convergence rate for the coordinate descent algorithm and develop efficient projection procedures with provable performance guarantees, addressing both the outer optimization and its necessary subproblems.

Numerical experiments focus on semi-supervised learning with hypergraphs. They confirm the algorithm's efficiency and show significant prediction-accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art methods in those experiments. These results connect the mathematical formulation to a practical learning outcome: the proposed optimization machinery supports effective prediction, as well as providing guarantees about how the solver progresses.
neurips-2018-quadratic-decomposable-subm.tldr: A new convex formulation for graph and hypergraph learning comes with efficient projection algorithms and a linearly convergent coordinate descent solver.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning requires decisions while knowledge is still incomplete, so uncertainty affects which experiences an agent gathers next. Methods designed to estimate uncertainty from a fixed dataset may be poorly suited to this sequential setting. The paper highlights a particular gap in bootstrap approaches: they have no mechanism for expressing uncertainty that does not originate in observed data.

The proposed remedy adds a randomly initialized, untrainable prior network to each member of an ensemble. These fixed random functions provide a source of uncertainty alongside the component learned from observations. The change is simple at the architectural level, but directly addresses the absence of uncertainty supplied independently of the collected dataset.

The authors prove efficiency for linear representations and give illustrative evidence of effectiveness with nonlinear representations. They also report substantially better scaling to large problems than previous attempts. The distinction between these findings matters: the formal efficiency result covers the linear setting, while nonlinear usefulness and large-scale behavior are supported by the reported demonstrations.
neurips-2018-randomized-prior-functions-.tldr: Adding a fixed random prior network to each ensemble member supplies uncertainty beyond observed data for reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: Automated theorem proving requires choosing promising steps within a difficult search space. This paper introduces a prover that uses practically no domain-specific heuristics to guide its connection-style proof search. Instead, it learns guidance from previous proof attempts, using reinforcement learning to direct many Monte Carlo simulations.

The authors construct several versions of the prover with different learning and search-guidance algorithms. Their strongest version is trained on a large collection of mathematical problems and then tested on problems it has not previously seen. This setup examines whether experience from earlier proof attempts can improve search on new mathematical tasks.

At the same inference budget, the trained system solves more than 40% more problems than the baseline prover. The equal number of inferences makes the reported improvement a gain in what the search achieves within that budget. The authors describe the result as, to their knowledge, the first convincing large-scale application of reinforcement learning to solving general mathematical problems.
neurips-2018-reinforcement-learning-of-t.tldr: A theorem prover learns search guidance from prior proof attempts and solves over 40% more problems than a baseline at the same inference budget.

paragraphs: Large observational datasets can support detailed predictions, but hidden confounding can undermine attempts to interpret those predictions causally. Unobserved influences may affect both the intervention received and its outcome. Experimental data avoids this confounding problem, yet is often available only for a smaller population or a narrower range of situations.

The paper proposes using limited experimental evidence to correct causal effect models learned from larger observational datasets. The method can work even when the two sources do not fully overlap. This makes the experiment an anchor for correcting the observational model, while retaining the broader information supplied by the observational data.

The authors state that their assumptions are strictly weaker than those of existing approaches and establish conditions under which the estimator is consistent. They also demonstrate effectiveness using real data from a large educational experiment. The consistency result is conditional on the proved conditions; the empirical application provides evidence that experimental grounding can usefully correct observational causal estimates.
neurips-2018-removing-hidden-confounding.tldr: Limited experimental data can correct hidden confounding in observational causal models, with consistency established under stated conditions.

paragraphs: A conditional generator is meant to produce samples matching a requested label. Randomly corrupted training labels can damage both label correctness and sample quality when a conditional GAN is trained conventionally. This paper develops methods for two cases: the label-noise distribution is either known in advance or must be learned.

With known noise, Robust Conditional GAN corrupts generated samples' labels before presenting them to the discriminator. Matching the noise channel on the generated side encourages the generator itself to represent clean labels. Multiplicative approximation bounds connect its loss to the distance between the clean data distribution and generated distribution, supporting robustness with a carefully chosen projection discriminator.

When the noise distribution is unknown, the RCGAN-U extension learns it alongside the generator. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 show consistent improvements over baseline approaches for both variants, with RCGAN-U performing close to RCGAN. The findings support explicitly modeling label corruption during adversarial training, while the theoretical robustness statement depends on the specified discriminator choice.
neurips-2018-robustness-of-conditional-g.tldr: Robust Conditional GAN models label corruption during adversarial training to learn cleaner conditional generators from noisy labels.

paragraphs: Detecting meaningful segments in a sequence requires understanding both the segments themselves and their wider context. Relationships among target segments can also matter. The Sequence-to-Segment Network addresses these needs with an end-to-end encoder-decoder architecture that converts an input sequence into a sequence of detected segments.

The encoder builds hidden states that progressively capture local information and an understanding of the whole input. A specialized decoder component, the Segment Detection Unit, combines these encoder states with its own state to detect segments one after another. This design lets segment detection draw on the sequence representation and the evolving decoding process together.

During training, predicted and reference segments are assigned through bipartite matching, and localization errors are measured using Earth Mover's Distance. These choices connect training to the task of matching sets of segments and placing them accurately. Experiments on temporal action proposal generation and video summarization report state-of-the-art performance on both tasks, supporting the architecture across two segment-selection applications.
neurips-2018-sequence-to-segment-network.tldr: Sequence-to-Segment Networks combine sequence-wide context with sequential decoding to detect segments effectively in action proposals and video summarization.

paragraphs: SING generates musical note waveforms from a requested instrument, pitch, and velocity. The paper targets the high computational cost of neural audio models that produce one sample at a time. Its alternative generates audio frame by frame with large strides, reducing the sequential work involved in synthesizing a note.

The model is lightweight and trained end to end, using one decoder for nearly 1,000 instruments. A new loss compares the log spectrograms of generated and target waveforms. This gives training a way to measure discrepancies in the spectral representations of the sounds while the model directly produces the waveform.

The evaluation tests pitch-and-instrument combinations absent from training. Compared with a state-of-the-art WaveNet-based autoencoder, SING achieves significantly better perceptual quality as measured by Mean Opinion Score. It is also reported to train about 32 times faster and perform inference about 2,500 times faster. These findings show that the frame-based approach can combine substantial speed gains with improved perceived quality on the stated generalization task.
neurips-2018-sing-symbol-to-instrument-n.tldr: SING synthesizes musical notes frame by frame, improving perceptual quality and greatly reducing computation in the reported WaveNet-autoencoder comparison.

paragraphs: Training uses gradients computed from a finite dataset, while the underlying learning objective concerns the full population. This paper studies how closely those gradients agree throughout nonconvex learning problems and what that agreement implies for optimization. It develops vector-valued Rademacher complexities as a composable tool for deriving uniform gradient bounds using norm-based capacity control.

For the smooth problems analyzed, the bounds can avoid explicit dependence on dimension. Applications include nonconvex generalized linear models and robust regression. The analysis shows how algorithms that find approximate stationary points can attain optimal sample complexity, even in high or potentially infinite dimension and when the dataset is reused for multiple passes.

The paper also identifies a sharp complication for nonsmooth models. Even a single ReLU cannot have dimension-independent gradient convergence rates in the worst case. A new distributional assumption restores dimension-independent rates. The results therefore explain both when gradient-based reasoning can support strong learning guarantees and why nonsmoothness requires additional care about the data distribution.
neurips-2018-uniform-convergence-of-grad.tldr: Uniform gradient bounds yield dimension-free learning guarantees for analyzed smooth problems, while ReLU models require additional distributional assumptions.
